In the rest of the continent Amazon does **not** operate a dedicated marketplace. Because of that, shoppers in those countries normally turn to local e‑commerce platforms such as Mercado Libre or Linio.  I don’t have a source that confirms this as of today, so you may want to check local consumer reviews or marketplace‑specific statistics for the most accurate picture.

answer_raw:
Amazon operates a local storefront only in **Brazil**; Amazon.com.br runs its own fulfillment centers and ships orders directly to cities such as São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro [7].  

In every other South American country—Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Uruguay, and Venezuela—Amazon does **not** have a dedicated marketplace. Customers can still shop via **Amazon International Shopping** (the successor to AmazonGlobal), but the items are shipped from the U.S. or other regional hubs, which results in longer delivery times and higher fees [3][7].  

Because of the lack of local fulfillment, shoppers in those countries usually turn to local e‑commerce platforms, though no source confirms which platforms are most popular.  

I don’t have a source confirming the specific local payment methods or tax‑compliance procedures Amazon uses in Brazil.
